messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 Incident created: Dedicated pool node fault detected in customer-dedicated pool for tenant Novanet (VPC-novanet-01). Auto-detect flagged GPU ECC errors and OOM events. Incident ID INC-20260301-94 · paging oncall: @alex_choi · link: https://infra.redwood/incident/INC-20260301-94

alex_choi: acked. I'm oncall and joining now. any initial impact notes?
marta_ops: Novanet reported 502s on a subset of their inference endpoints ~5m ago, metrics show increased queueing on pool-ded-82. GPU 0 on node gpu-node-137 reporting ECC and then driver reset.
ryan_eng: seeing telemetry: kernel crashes -> nvml reports ECC single-bit -> then uncorrectable? logs attached in incident timeline. Looks like CUDA driver panic followed by container evictions.

sam_solutions: customer is mid-rollout, they're using reserved capacity in VPC; they asked to avoid tenant-wide reassign if possible. They prefer warm handoff to fallback capacity in us-east-1.
olivia_cust-liaison: I just told Novanet we’ve acknowledged and are isolating the affected hardware; they asked for ETA and whether data is at risk.
alex_choi: mitigation plan: 1) cordon & drain node gpu-node-137; 2) reroute Novanet traffic to their fallback pool (ded-pool-novanet-02) with temporary capacity bump; 3) kick hardware replacement flow with vendor; 4) monitor quality/regressions. Anyone object?
liz_infra: no objections. I can do the drain and trigger replacement. note: draining will evict a handful of long-lived KV-cache sessions; we should signal the service to flush prefix caches first.
ryan_eng: +1. Suggest we set a short client-facing degrade policy so requests return 429 rather than hang if queueing spikes. Also enable trace sampling for Novanet for 30m.
alex_choi: OK executing step 1 now. running:`kubectl cordon gpu-node-137 && kubectl drain gpu-node-137 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m`
deploy-bot: :rocket: drain job started for gpu-node-137 by alex_choi at 2026-03-01T21:05:03Z. Job ID: drain-1769002345-1
marta_ops: starting cache flush for Novanet prefixes: sending soft clear to redis-kv-novanet: `FLUSHDB ASYNC` for non-critical tenants, and `EVICT_PATTERN novanet:*` for others.
olivia_cust-liaison: Novanet acknowledged and asked to be kept in loop. they also requested logs for RCA when available.
ryan_eng: Drain progressing; 3 pods rescheduled to ded-pool-novanet-02, 2 pods still terminating due to large in-memory KV snapshots. considering forcing eviction at 5m if not cleared.
alex_choi: forcing eviction in 2m if still stuck. alerting oncall to expect short 1-2 min 5xx spike during final kill.
marta_ops: pushed scaledown protection for their primary router so we don't accidentally scale down healthy workers during drain.
liz_infra: replacement ticket created with vendor (ticket REF-99321). Vendor ETA 8 hours for HW swap but they can hot-swap NVMe/PSU earlier if needed. I'm requesting advance replacement priority due to customer SLA.
sam_solutions: Novanet wants to avoid cross-region fallback if possible. Confirming they accept routing to ded-pool-novanet-02 (same region) with extra capacity.
ryan_eng: one long-lived pod still stuck in Terminating due to blocked finalizer (kv-checkpoint). I can exec in and trigger checkpoint upload to S3 to speed it up. Proceeding.
alex_choi: go for it. keep me posted.
ryan_eng: checkpoint uploaded, pod terminated. drain completed. deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: drain job finished for gpu-node-137 (duration 9m12s).
marta_ops: traffic rerouted to ded-pool-novanet-02 and autoscaler bumped by +30% for 20m. Observability: latency returned to baseline within 2 minutes, error rate peaked at 7% for 90s.
olivia_cust-liaison: relaying to Novanet: brief error spike, all traffic now on fallback pool, vendor swap requested, will provide ETA. they asked for a post-incident timeline.
alex_choi: tagging follow-ups: - hw-replace owner: liz_infra - postmortem owner: ryan_eng - customer comms: olivia_cust-liaison - metrics/regression: marta_ops
liz_infra: vendor confirmed parts in transit; field tech ETA 6.5 hours now. I'll schedule on-prem engineer to do onsite swap and power cycle.
sam_solutions: question: do we want automatic fallback to pool-compat when a node-level failure occurs? currently we only fallback at pool-level. Thinking about a short-term tweak to routing policy to prefer non-draining nodes without manual ops.
ryan_eng: that's a product discussion but for now let's note it as a follow-up. We should document the drain->fallback playbook for VPC/reserved customers.
alex_choi: adding a temporary incident note to the customer's SLA tracker. Also enabling verbose logging for 1h to capture any regression.
marta_ops: checks: model quality sampling shows no significant degradation (BLEU/ROUGE stable) for the sampled requests. embeddings pipeline unaffected.
olivia_cust-liaison: Novanet asked if we can provide logs for the evicted containers. I've granted them read-only access to the incident bucket and uploaded compressed logs: s3://incidents/INC-20260301-94/logs.tar.gz
ryan_eng: hardware diag: GPU thermal sensors show transient overtemp, fan tach spikes followed by driver reset. Likely a failing fan or thermal paste issue causing runaway temps under burst. Sending telem to vendor.
liz_infra: opening a preventive ticket to scan remaining nodes in pool for fan and thermal anomalies.
sam_solutions: customer requested estimated downtime if hardware replacement takes longer. I told them we expect no downtime beyond the near-term 2-3 minute spike, since we routed to fallback pool, but final resolution depends on vendor ETA.
alex_choi: preparing handoff to morning oncall. Summary: drain completed, traffic routed, replacement in progress (vendor ETA ~6.5h), customer notified, monitoring in place. Oncall to watch for: re-queue spikes, unusual cache misses, repeated ECC counts on sibling GPUs.
ryan_eng: posting quick runbook snippet for ops team to accelerate future drains:
```
# drain fast checklist
1. signal app to persist in-memory KV to S3
2. run `kubectl drain NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m`
3. bump fallback pool autoscaler +30%
4. enable 1m sample tracing for affected tenant
5. confirm client timeouts are set to 10s to fail fast
```

marta_ops: adding alert rule to watch ECC uncorrectable > 1 -> auto-schedule maintenance.
olivia_cust-liaison: Novanet replied: thanks, appreciated the quick response. asking for scheduled maintenance window to replace node to avoid surprises. I asked vendor to coordinate with customer for a 2-hour window tomorrow.
alex_choi: ok I'll mark incident as 'mitigated' and hand off to liz_infra for vendor coordination and ryan_eng for postmortem. Oncall says we'll keep the thread open until vendor confirms swap.
deploy-bot: :information_source: incident INC-20260301-94 status updated to MITIGATED by alex_choi at 2026-03-02T03:12:00Z
liz_infra: vendor confirmed field tech arriving tomorrow 09:00 local, will attempt hot-swap and thermal paste rework. scheduling maintenance window with Novanet.
ryan_eng: taking postmortem ownership. I'll collect logs, timelines, and follow-up action items (thermal sensor baseline, replacement SOP, and routing policy doc). ETA for draft: 48h.

alex_choi: thanks everyone. handing off oncall to morning pager @marta_ops. please escalate if regressions appear. :thumbsup:
